llm-app-serving.title: Serving an LLM app
llm-app-serving.description: Client → API → inference → post-process — where latency and failure land.

steps.heading: Typical serve path
steps.caption: Request path — the browser never talks to the model vendor with your secret keys; your backend does.

steps.heading: Pattern choice
steps.caption: Sync vs async — short completions can block an HTTP request; long jobs need queues and webhooks.

steps.heading: Queue depth under spike
steps.caption: Backpressure — when inference saturates, queue or shed load; do not unbounded-accept until OOM.

steps.heading: Minimum production gates
steps.caption: Checklist — auth, timeouts, token caps, logging of prompt hashes / ids, and graceful vendor errors.

fastapi-role.title: FastAPI’s role
fastapi-role.description: A Python API layer for validation, auth, and orchestration — not the model itself.

steps.heading: POST /v1/chat
steps.caption: Route — validate body, authenticate, then call a service that talks to the model.

steps.heading: Layering
steps.caption: Keep routes thin — business rules and prompts live in services/modules you can unit test without HTTP.

steps.heading: SSE stream
steps.caption: Streaming — yield SSE/chunks from an async generator so clients see tokens early.

steps.heading: Do / don’t
steps.caption: FastAPI is one good option among many — the pattern (typed API gateway) matters more than the brand.

docker.title: Docker for LLM apps
docker.description: Package API + workers with locked dependencies — same artifact from laptop to server.

steps.heading: Build
steps.caption: Image — build a reproducible filesystem with your app and dependencies.

steps.heading: Runtime config
steps.caption: Run — container gets CPU/memory limits, env for API keys, and mounts for caches if needed.

steps.heading: Compose services
steps.caption: Multi-service — API, worker, and maybe a local redis compose together for dev parity.

steps.heading: Image size (illustrative)
steps.caption: Models in images — shipping multi-GB weights bloats deploys; prefer pull-at-start or remote inference.

kubernetes-overview.title: Kubernetes overview for LLM apps
kubernetes-overview.description: Pods, services, and autoscaling — orchestration when one VM is no longer enough.

steps.heading: Pools
steps.caption: Workload split — stateless API Deployment vs GPU worker Deployment on a separate node pool.

steps.heading: Traffic
steps.caption: Service discovery — ClusterIP/Ingress fronts the API; workers pull from a queue rather than taking public traffic.

steps.heading: Probe pitfalls
steps.caption: Probes — liveness ≠ “can finish a 60s generation.” Use startup probes and separate readiness from long jobs.

steps.heading: Workers vs queue lag
steps.caption: Autoscaling signal — RPS for APIs; queue lag or GPU util for workers. Wrong signal → thrash or starvation.

bedrock.title: Amazon Bedrock (conceptual)
bedrock.description: Managed foundation models via AWS APIs — IAM, regions, and serverless invocation.

steps.heading: InvokeModel / Converse
steps.caption: Invoke — your service calls Bedrock with IAM credentials; model id selects the backend foundation model.

steps.heading: Enterprise levers
steps.caption: Controls — VPC endpoints, SCPs, and CloudTrail matter as much as prompt quality in enterprises.

steps.heading: Common pattern
steps.caption: RAG on AWS — often pair Bedrock with a vector store (OpenSearch, etc.) you operate or buy.

steps.heading: Abstraction
steps.caption: Portability — keep prompts/tools behind an interface so Bedrock is a provider, not your architecture.

vertex-ai.title: Vertex AI (conceptual)
vertex-ai.description: Google Cloud’s managed ML/LLM platform — endpoints, Model Garden, and Gemini APIs.

steps.heading: GenerateContent-style path
steps.caption: Call path — app in GCP (or elsewhere) invokes a Vertex generative / prediction API with Google auth.

steps.heading: Managed vs deployed
steps.caption: Deployed endpoints — for custom/self-hosted models on Vertex, you manage machine type and autoscaling.

steps.heading: Grounded answer path
steps.caption: Data grounding — Vertex offers grounding/search integrations; still verify citations in your app layer.

steps.heading: Own these
steps.caption: Same lesson as other clouds — wrap the SDK; own evals, budgets, and PII handling.

azure-ai.title: Azure AI (conceptual)
azure-ai.description: Azure OpenAI / AI Studio patterns — resource deployment, keys/RBAC, and content filters.

steps.heading: Chat completions
steps.caption: Deployment model — you call a deployment name in a resource/region, not a raw open model slug alone.

steps.heading: Hitting TPM
steps.caption: Capacity — TPM/RPM quotas are per deployment. Spikes need either higher quota or queueing.

steps.heading: Error classes
steps.caption: Content filtering — platform may block or modify outputs; log filter results separately from model errors.

steps.heading: Auth posture
steps.caption: Enterprise networking — private endpoints and Managed Identity beat shipping keys in env files.

streaming.title: Streaming tokens
streaming.description: Send partial tokens as they decode — better UX, harder cancellation and billing accounting.

steps.heading: Perceived progress
steps.caption: Buffered vs streamed — waiting for the full completion feels slower even when total time is equal.

steps.heading: SSE deltas
steps.caption: Protocol — often SSE or WebSocket; each event carries a delta string.

steps.heading: Disconnect handling
steps.caption: Cancel — if the user navigates away, abort the provider stream to stop burning tokens.

steps.heading: Filter timing
steps.caption: Post-filters — some safety checks need the full text; others can scan incrementally. Design explicitly.

monitoring-basics.title: Monitoring basics for LLM apps
monitoring-basics.description: RED/USE plus LLM-specific signals — latency, tokens, error classes, and quality samples.

steps.heading: p95 latency
steps.caption: Classic API metrics still apply — if p95 latency explodes, users leave before “quality” matters.

steps.heading: Daily tokens by type
steps.caption: Token economics — input vs output tokens drive cost; alert on spend anomalies per tenant.

steps.heading: Error budget burn
steps.caption: Error taxonomy — separate rate limits, timeouts, content filters, tool failures, and 5xx.

steps.heading: Feedback loop
steps.caption: Quality sampling — log traces (prompt id, retrieval ids) and score a sample daily.
